newsitem.title: TURKEY: Seven Turkish police suspended in security scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seven Turkish police suspended in security scandal.

text.p: Turkish Interior Minister Meral Aksener has suspended seven police officers in a security scandal over alleged links between authorities and organised crime, the interior ministry said in a statement on Thursday.

The seven, from different units in central and southern Turkey, are being questioned over claims they deliberately made no efffort to arrest fugitive gangster Mehmet Ozcan and that they aided and abetted convicted criminals.
The Radikal newpaper said on Wednesday that a criminal gang headed by Ozcan had at one time been led by Abdullah Catli, a late mobster at the centre of the scandal.
Convicted heroin-smuggler Catli, who had been wanted for murder for 18 years, died last month in a traffic accident in the same car as a senior policeman and a government MP.
The subsequent scandal led to the resignation of Aksener's predecessor at the interior ministry and the suspension of Istanbul police chief Kemal Yazicioglu.
The media says security officials and politicians have turned a blind eye to underworld activities and used gangsters to kill political opponents and business rivals.
